title: Governed public proof-of-work Build Log
summary: Launched a public proof-of-work Build Log, added local and live rendering checks, surfaced it from the portfolio home, and made the public-repository disclosure boundary explicit so unadmitted publication candidates stay on the private side of the workflow.
why_it_matters: It creates a practical way to turn verified work into external evidence without turning private planning, session telemetry or raw activity into a public feed.

title: Interactive solution-space atlas
summary: Shipped an interactive map that lets visitors explore reusable capability combinations by problem, lifecycle stage and scale, with direct routes into the underlying method profiles.
why_it_matters: It turns a large method catalogue into a problem-first proof surface, making the work easier to understand, navigate and reuse without presenting capability membership as a score or maturity claim.

title: Capability inventory and problem-space map
summary: Reconciled the public methods catalogue into a broader capability inventory, added public-safe capability profiles and introduced a problem-first map connecting reusable capabilities to concrete problem classes.
why_it_matters: It makes a growing capability estate understandable from the problem being solved rather than requiring visitors to already know internal method or project names.

title: When a Rule Is Not a Control
summary: Published a technical guide on separating instruction, authority, enforcement, verification and preservation when AI agents can change real state, including bounded behavioural evidence from the implementation case.
why_it_matters: It turns a concrete governance failure mode into a reusable engineering distinction: telling an agent the rule is not the same thing as enforcing the boundary.

title: Rules, Authority & Enforcement reader labs
summary: Shipped interactive synthetic reader labs for exploring the difference between an instruction, actual authority, enforcement, verification and preservation in agentic systems, with dedicated browser interaction checks.
why_it_matters: The labs make an abstract governance distinction testable and teachable: a documented rule, permission boundary and effective control are separate engineering properties.

title: Public portfolio landing with live Pages acceptance
summary: Unified the GitHub Pages root into a public portfolio landing, repaired interaction failures across the earlier method profiles, added browser regression coverage, and extended acceptance checks to the externally deployed Pages site with a durable status receipt.
why_it_matters: It separates repository success from user-visible success: the portfolio is not treated as delivered merely because files merged, but is checked through the interface visitors actually use.

title: Ten interactive method and protocol profiles
summary: Completed a public series of ten interactive, source-pinned profiles covering 5PP, Dialogue Lifecycle, ORBIT, AICS, DIALECTIC, RigVedan, Hermeneutic-Didactic, DIAL-4, DIAL-4+ and DIAL-4P Possibility, with explicit evidence boundaries and synthetic laboratories.
why_it_matters: It turns method documentation into inspectable proof surfaces that show mechanisms, provenance, boundaries and experiments instead of asking readers to trust prose alone.

title: Broker Lane Sandbox source-first evidence card
summary: Published a source-first evidence card for Broker Lane Sandbox that orients visitors around a public default-deny execution boundary while keeping security claims and source authority explicitly bounded.
why_it_matters: It demonstrates how a safety-oriented capability can be explained and evidenced publicly without exposing private implementation state or turning orientation material into stronger security claims than the sources support.
